summary.text: A 68-year-old postmenopausal woman with diabetes and hypertension presented with a right axillary lump the size of a small tennis ball of 1 week's duration. The lump was well circumscribed, tender, mobile, rubbery and about 5 × 5 × 4 cm, with non-contributory general and systemic examination and no organomegaly.

Workup showed hemoglobin 8.9g/dl and normal LDH, and axillary ultrasonography revealed multiple hypoechoic cystic areas. The aspirate was suppurative and suggestive of an infective pathology. Excision biopsy showed an effaced lymph node with sheets of predominantly large cells, necrosis, brisk mitoses, and a Ki 67 labeling index of 70%.

Immunohistochemistry was positive for CD 20, PAX5, Oct 2 and BOB 1 and also for CD 43, CD 4, CD 2, CD 7 and weak aberrant CD 3, with EBER negative. The final diagnosis was diffuse large B cell lymphoma with aberrant expression of T cell-associated antigens.
She received 4 cycles of R-CHOP-based chemotherapy and was evaluated as having a partial response to therapy, after which she was lost to follow-up.
